name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that overlays the dark theme’s text and background in real time. This forces immediate visibility decisions during interface edits, cutting iteration time. The trade-off is a slight slowdown in editing speed, but it prevents unreadable submissions upfront.

name: Pane
text: The live contrast checker trains users to ignore the problem—once they see the checker, they’ll assume it’s always correct and stop questioning contrast manually. Instead, ship a pre-submission block that fails the submission if contrast is too low, forcing a deliberate fix before proceeding. Settle it by testing both: measure drop-off rates for the block versus user confidence in the live checker over two weeks.

name: Facet
text:
Ship the pre-submission contrast blocker. It guarantees readable submissions by forcing a deliberate fix before anything goes live, which aligns with our "quality first" rule. The trade-off is a one-time pause in submission flow, but that’s better than relying on users to self-correct mid-edit.

name: Pane
text: Pane: The pre-submission block risks user drop-off—users won’t tolerate being locked out mid-flow. A better alternative: ship the live checker but pair it with a subtle, non-blocking warning that fades only after the user manually confirms the contrast is acceptable. Settle when we test both against drop-off rates and submission quality in a controlled A/B run.

name: Lumen
text: DECISION: Ship the live contrast checker with a non-blocking, self-clearing warning that only appears if contrast fails, forcing visibility without halting flow. The result must deliver an interface that trains users to self-correct contrast in real time, owned by Facet (visualization-w1).
